personas.name: An inference provider
personas.blurb: you sell tokens. Your margin is GPU cost per token, so the optimisation and compute boxes are your stack, and routers are your distribution.

personas.name: An AI product company
personas.blurb: token spend is your COGS. Model choice, routing, compression and caching decide gross margin; evals and memory decide quality.

personas.name: A large enterprise adopting AI
personas.blurb: you buy outcomes. Most value flows through apps, platforms and services partners; governance and security are the gate.

personas.name: A GPU cloud / neocloud
personas.blurb: you turn capital and power into rentable clusters. Power, financing and allocation of GPUs are the constraints; marketplaces are a channel.

personas.name: A model lab
personas.blurb: compute and data are your inputs. Expert data and RL environments are now as contested as GPUs.

personas.name: An individual developer
personas.blurb: you adopt bottom-up. Coding agents, open models, local runtimes and pay-as-you-go APIs are your stack.

personas.name: An AI chip company
personas.blurb: you live on foundry, packaging and HBM allocation. The software stack decides whether anyone can use your silicon.

personas.name: An AI services / transformation firm
personas.blurb: you sit between technology and outcomes. Your leverage is knowing which boxes a client actually needs.

changelog.text: 8 additions, 5 acquisitions/mergers, 1 shutdown, 11 corrections, 18 funding updates. Highlights: Qualcomm bought RISC-V CPU designer Akeana and Infineon completed C2i Semiconductors; Tenstorrent ($1.5B Series E), FuriosaAI (KRW 820B Series D) and Labelbox (Series E) raised; Deepgram agreed to buy Daily, steward of Pipecat; Google is folding Jules into Antigravity; LMArena is now Arena and Intercom is now Fin; new listings include General Compute, Akamai's inference service, Mintive, Town, Serval, Greptile, AISLE and AuxoAI.
Atlas published: 12 links in the chain, 171 segments, 1,860 companies, 453 open projects, standards and public programmes, 67 investors.
